S&P DOW JONES INDICES AND KALSHI PARTNER TO CREATE NEW FINANCIAL INDICES S&P DJI will develop indices powered by Kalshi’s prediction markets. Potential markets include politics, AI job disruption, sports, economic indicators, and weather. The indices could enable investors to gain exposure to real-world events and hedge risk through linked financial products. Over $20 trillion is benchmarked to S&P DJI indices. The partnership could bring prediction markets closer to mainstream finance. Source:

GLOBAL INFLATION RISKS RISE DESPITE RESILIENT ECONOMIC GROWTH A Reuters poll of more than 500 economists found that 2027 inflation forecasts were raised for 31 of 50 economies, as oil prices above $100 per barrel fuel persistent price pressures. Meanwhile, AI investment is supporting economic resilience, with global growth forecasts upgraded to 3.0% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027.

NETANYAHU FACES ELECTION SETBACK AS ISRAELI EXIT POLLS SHOW DEADLOCK Israeli exit polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc running neck and neck with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, with neither side projected to secure the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. Voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades. Arab parties could hold the balance of power, although coalition negotiations remain complicated.

US IRAN WAR COSTS SURPASS $47 BILLION, PENTAGON ESTIMATES The US military has spent more than $47 billion on the war in Iran, according to Pentagon data reviewed by Reuters, exceeding the Defense Department’s July estimate by over 25%. The costs include more than $29 billion to replenish munitions and over $6 billion to replace military equipment. The estimate does not clearly account for repairs to US bases damaged by Iranian missile and drone attacks.

GOLDMAN SACHS SEES LIMITED FED HIKES, POTENTIAL STOCK MARKET RALLY Goldman Sachs expects just one additional Fed rate hike, compared with three currently priced by markets, suggesting the current tightening cycle could be among the smallest since 1983. Strategist Vickie Chang highlighted historically strong equity performance following limited tightening cycles: the S&P 500 gained 34% in the year after the 1997 hike and 9% following the 2015 hike.

INVESTORS PULL $18.5 BILLION FROM US STOCKS IN TWO WEEKS Bank of America clients sold a net $3.5 billion in US equities last week, following $15 billion in outflows the previous week. According to BofA analysts Jill Carey Hall and Trey Brown, retail investors led the selling. Communication services recorded its largest weekly outflow since tracking began in 2018, affecting a sector that includes Meta ($META). Industrials also faced heavy selling, marking their 13th consecutive week of outflows.
